description: Hi! I'm War from Malaysia (GMT+8), joining via the Universal Event. I'm building an interactive detective game where kids uncover the stories and science behind the machines NASA left on the Moon and Mars.
summary:
Space Sleuths is an interactive detective game that introduces young space fans to machines NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars. Players open case files on five pieces of hardware: the Spirit and Opportunity rovers, the Ingenuity helicopter, the Apollo 11 gear left on the Moon, and the Apollo 11 laser reflector. In each case they inspect clues, guess what happened, then uncover the real story and the science the machine made possible.

It answers the challenge by turning “abandoned” equipment into memorable stories, covering both silent machines and one still working today. It matters because kids don’t just read facts, they reason from evidence like real scientists, and every fact links back to its NASA source.
details:
What it does: Space Sleuths is a browser detective game for school age space fans. Players open five case files on machines NASA left on the Moon and Mars: the Spirit rover, the Opportunity rover, the Ingenuity helicopter, the gear Apollo 11 left on the Moon, and the Apollo 11 laser reflector. In each case they inspect three clues, make a guess, see what really happened, then learn what the machine discovered.

How it is creative: Two cases break the pattern. In Pack the Lander, players decide what Apollo 11 leaves behind so Eagle is light enough to lift off, then learn the real crew threw out their backpacks and overshoes to carry Moon rocks home. In The Mirror Panel, every answer is wrong, because the laser reflector was never abandoned and is still used today to show the Moon drifts 3.8 cm a year.

Benefits and impact: Kids reason from evidence like scientists instead of just reading facts. The game covers both silent and still working hardware on two worlds, and every fact links to its NASA or JPL source.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript on GitHub Pages. NASA photos turned into illustrations with a Python OpenCV filter. Sound effects and space ambience generated in code with the Web Audio API.

What we considered: Readability for young players (Atkinson Hyperlegible font), phones and computers, reduced motion settings, and keeping every fact accurate and sourced.
